about: The landing page's Recently Added list, newest first; the page shows the first four. Add an entry whenever a batch gives players something new to find: a dungeon, a mode, a family of items, a system. Every GREENSHORE_STORY_VERSION from firstTrackedRulesVersion on must be named here, by an entry's rulesVersion or in notNews (a bump players would not call news). spacetimedb/test/landing_news.test.ts holds that. Write it the way a player would say it.

entries.title: Ornament kits
entries.text: Every boss can now drop a Gilded Ornament Kit, very rarely: about one boss kill in a thousand. Put it on any piece of gear to give it a gold finish that everyone sees, in duels and in co-op too. It changes only how the piece looks, and you can take it off again any time to get the kit back. Kits trade on the Market, and each boss page in the Collection Log has a slot for one.

entries.title: More of your gear works in co-op
entries.text: Champion's Lure, Overkill, Retaliation, Shield Bash and the King's Amulet now work in co-op. The party fights on the best Lure anyone brings, so champions turn up more often for everyone. Overkill carries your extra damage into the next monster, Retaliation and Shield Bash hit the party's monster back, and the King's Amulet pays you its coins from every kill you helped with. Region diary tasks count in co-op too: the kills you land, and the fights you get through without being hit.

entries.title: Marked hunts and trophies
entries.text: Two new unlocks in the Bounty shop. Target scent makes your bounty's target turn up twice as often. Marked hunts make it more likely to be a champion, and every Marked champion drops a trophy only bounties give: a Grave Tooth, a Slime Core, a Wanted Poster and more, or a Hunter's Trophy from a boss. Trade them, sell them, or turn them in to Rook for Marks. Both work with a friend too.

entries.title: The Bounty shop
entries.text: Spend your Marks at Rook's shop. Unlock a second and third offer to choose from, twists that pay more, blocks for targets you never want, longer bounties and a second free new offer a day. Climb the bounty ranks to open more of the shop, and earn the Hunter's Ring tier by tier: it hits champions harder, finds more of them and doubles some loot while you hold a bounty. It can't be traded, and it's never lost in the Dark. Reach rank 10 for the Bounty Hunter badge.

entries.title: Bounties
entries.text: Rook has opened a Bounty Board in the QUESTS menu once you finish the Greenshore Story. Take a bounty, hunt its target in the Endless Dungeon, on your own or with a friend. Kills in the Dark count twice. Turn it in for Marks, a chest and some experience, and save the Marks for the Bounty shop. Keep a streak going: every 10th bounty in a row pays three times the Marks and a better chest.

entries.title: Watch your runs again
entries.text: Your runs are kept now, so you can watch them back. Open REPLAYS from the main menu, or press WATCH REPLAY on the results card. Play, pause, step one piece at a time, scrub to any fight and change the speed. Your 10 newest runs are kept, plus the run behind each of your records, and you can star up to 5 more to keep. Save a replay as a file to show someone, and load one back to watch it.

entries.title: Pets in co-op and duels
entries.text: Your pets now help in co-op too. The boss pets steer the whole party's Endless Dungeon toward their homes, and a Little Slime King anywhere in the party makes golden Slime Kings twice as likely for everyone. The Pet Cultist's portal opens in duels as well, half as often as against monsters. And the Pet Entling and the Little Garbage Man now work in Farm versus rooms.

entries.title: Boss pets do things now
entries.text: The three boss pets help now. The Little Slime King leads you to the Slime Grotto more often and makes golden Slime Kings twice as likely. The Little Cyclops brings an extra Eye Ball from every kill that drops them, sometimes doubles a champion's loot, and finds the Cyclops Arena more often. The Little Garbage Man gets you a quarter more Gold from Farm garbage, digs up Scrap from your kills, gets you into his dungeon for 3 Scrap, and finds the Dump more often.

entries.title: Restricted accounts
entries.text: Start a new character as a restricted account and make or find everything yourself: no Player Market, friendly Arena fights only, and nothing taken from players you beat in the Dark. A padlock shows beside your name in chat, on friends' lists and in duels, and at level 30 you earn a skin only restricted players get. You can leave any time, but you can't come back.

entries.title: Pets
entries.text: Pets have arrived. A very rare kill can drop one: a little Zombie, Bandit, Cultist or Oak Entling, or one of the Slime King, the Cyclops and the Garbage Man. Hollis has a dog called Cubey for you too. Put your pet in the new Pet slot at the top of your Boosts and it follows you into every fight and around the Farm. Some help: the Zombie hits the undead harder, the Bandit brings more coins, the Cultist's portal sometimes strikes twice, the Entling finds more wood and Cubey sniffs out other pets. Pets can't be traded, and if you ever let one go you can claim it back from the new PETS tab of the Collection Log.

entries.title: Tonics and two new foods
entries.text: The Cookhouse brews tonics now. Put one in your aid slot and your next dungeon run gets a Forge effect on top of your gear: more damage, fewer big hits, more against champions, more experience, more coins or double loot. One is used up by every dungeon run you start with it. And two new foods: an Emergency Ration that saves you once when you drop to 10% health, and Trail Mix that tops you up a little at a time from 80%.

entries.title: Region diaries
entries.text: Every region of the Endless Dungeon has a diary in the Region Log: Easy, Medium, Hard and Elite tasks built around what lives there. Beat 50 Bandits in Bandit Camp, kill the Bandit King with a T-Spin, finish the Cult Leader with a clear that takes your bottom row, or take down the Slime King with his walls, slime and envelop all on you. Each tier pays that region's charts, Medium and Elite add a chest, Hard earns the region's badge and a free chart every day, and every Elite diary makes you a Pathfinder.

entries.title: Badges
entries.text: Finish the whole Collection Log, every feat, every quest, every region of the Endless Dungeon, every challenge skin or every Build node and you earn a badge. Reach level 10 in all three masteries for Grandmaster, and everyone playing now is a Beta Player. Pick one to show in chat beside your level, on your friends' lists and on the duel intro. See all your badges, and how close you are to the rest, on the new BADGES tab of the Collection Log, and look at a friend's from their menu. A finished log page now turns gold with a seal.

entries.title: Loadouts and Respec Orbs
entries.text: Save your gear, food and boosts as named loadouts and put one on with a single press, from your bag or right before a run. Any enemy in a dungeon can now drop a Respec Orb. It's very rare, more likely from bosses, champions and the Dark, and more likely the deeper you go. Use one in the Combat or Skills tree to get every point back, or to start a new saved build. You can keep three builds in each tree, and at level 50 the Scrap Forge breaks an orb into ten Respec Shards, one for each switch between them.

entries.title: A Forge roll worth watching
entries.text: Rolling at the Scrap Forge is a show now. The glow builds, the modifiers flicker past and land on yours, and the stars climb to its grade, each grade with its own colour and sound. A IV gets the full celebration. Rerolls tell you what you are giving up and whether you went up or down. Click to skip. III and IV gear catches the light in your bag. The odds are exactly as they were.

entries.title: Tell us what you'd add
entries.text: The main menu has a HELP button. Send us your ideas, anything that feels missing, or a bug, straight from the game. Or open the new How to Play guide.

entries.title: Onslaught waits a round longer
entries.text: Onslaught now starts a round later, at the 25th fight, on your own, in Dark and with a friend.

entries.title: Tier-four armour finds its place
entries.text: Lotus and orichalcum armour has been rebalanced, so every tier-four piece is worth wearing.

entries.title: Rival boards move when a piece lands
entries.text: The boards of the other players in Farm Versus, a duel or a co-op run now change when they place a piece, rather than showing their piece falling. You still see every stack, line clear and attack as it happens.

entries.title: Omens with a friend
entries.text: Omens now work in co-op Endless, for both of you.

entries.title: Thorns and staggers with a friend, and healing in duels
entries.text: With a friend, the Cultist's Amulet's tentacle, Staggering and Interrupting now hold back or call off the monster's attack just as they do on your own, and the Ring of Thorns and Thorned hurt it back whenever it hits you. Thorns still never land the killing blow. In a duel, Regenerating and Tranquil now heal you, at half their usual amount.

entries.title: Shields, dodges and parries in duels
entries.text: Block, Spin Ward, Dodge and Parry now work when you fight another player. Block and Spin Ward raise a shield that stops your opponent's next hit whole, and a shield you already have up when a duel starts comes into the fight with you. Dodge can take a hit's damage away, and Parry can keep it off your board. In a duel Block, Dodge and Parry each have half their usual chance, and a shield that goes into a duel stays there, so it can't also stop the next monster.

entries.title: Bags that keep what you found, and jewellery in co-op
entries.text: When you die in the Dark Endless Dungeon, a Rugged Satchel or Slime Bag now keeps from what you really found: region chests, boss drops and omen drops included. The satchel keeps whatever would sell for the most, so it no longer saves a potion over a weapon. The Garbage Man's dump no longer uses up a Provisions Pouch, since you can't eat there. And with a friend, the Ring of Garbage, the Hourglass Amulet and Tactician now hold the monster's attack back just as they do on your own.

entries.title: A calm before the King, and more Bandit Elites
entries.text: The Slime King's pit now opens on a few seconds of calm: build up your board while his music plays softly, then he walks in and his walls bring the drums. With a friend, you both get the same calm. And in the Endless Dungeon the bandits get tougher the deeper you go: Bandit Elites start turning up in the Bandit Camp from your fourth region on, until most of its bandits are elites, and the Bandit Town fields even more of them than before.

entries.title: A funky song for the shops
entries.text: The Store, your bag, crafting, the Collection Log and Skins have a song of their own now: a laid-back, funky groove that swells in the moment you open one. Upgrades and Settings keep their calmer tune.

entries.title: The Slime King’s song
entries.text: The Slime King has his own music. A low, bubbling groove plays while you wait for him and between kings, and the moment he slams his walls down the whole band kicks in. When he falls it drops back, carrying right on from where it was.

entries.title: A song for the menus
entries.text: LDBG has a second song. Settle into Settings, your upgrades, crafting, your bag, the Store, the Collection Log or Skins and a slower, gentler tune swells in to keep you company. Head back to the title and the calm loop swells back. It only changes once you stay on a screen for a moment, so popping in and out doesn't keep swapping songs.

entries.title: A faster start
entries.text: The game's first download is about a quarter smaller: the moving picture behind the activity list is gone, and the list now stands in the main menu's tower instead. Craft, your Inventory, Skins and the Collection Log are made ready behind the loading screen, so they open straight away the first time, and fights run smoother on slower computers.

entries.title: Better chests in the Dark
entries.text: Chests in the Dark Endless Dungeon now come better as well as bigger: half of each chest's chance moves up a tier, so every region's chests are much likelier to be a tier up than they are in Endless, and the Cultist Tower's Royal Chest turns up more than twice as often. They still pay double. Arcane Vaults and Royal Chests stay in the hardest regions.

entries.title: The Dark Endless Dungeon
entries.text: Dark has moved into the Endless Dungeon. The same regions, at Dark strength: enemies hit twice as hard, every kill rolls its drops three times, and ordinary chests pay double, with Dark chests holding what other players lost. Leave at a checkpoint to keep your haul. Die to a monster and you lose what you found and your gear breaks, and other players can find you between fights. Charts and Omens work here too. Dark Greenshore is retired: Greenshore is its Story now.

entries.title: Story and Challenges
entries.text: The dungeon list is tidier. STORY holds Greenshore, the Endless Dungeon has a card of its own with Dark Endless beside it, and CHALLENGES holds the Garbage Man and the Slime King, with their fees and bests as before. One OMENS switch sits above the Endless cards, and the Region Log is a single button.

entries.title: Charts
entries.text: Build the Cartographer's Table to draw charts for the Endless Dungeon. Put a chart in your new map slot and your run heads for that region: it's there the first time its tier can come up, and keeps turning up more often after. A chart is only used if you actually get there. You can only chart a region you've already found, and each chart is made from what that region drops.

entries.title: A sturdier look
entries.text: Buttons, cards and windows stand on cleaner, solid bottoms, the gold dividers meet their diamonds properly, and the panels around a dungeon board are far less see-through. And the Cyclops finally has fists to match Punchy, Shooty and Bernie.

entries.title: Music
entries.text: LDBG has its own soundtrack. A calm loop plays on the title and the menus, and when you step into the Farm or a dungeon the full theme kicks in and keeps going from one activity to the next. Finish a dungeon run and the theme plays out to its ending. Top out, die or lose a duel, and it stops dead with a boom, then the calm loop fades back in for your next try. Changes always land on the beat. Turn it up or down with the Music slider in Settings.

entries.title: The Region Log
entries.text: The Endless Dungeon now remembers where you have been. The first time you walk into a region, NEW REGION is stamped over its banner. Open the Region Log from the Endless Dungeon card to see every region: the ones you have found, with who lives there, what they drop and how deep you got, the ones still waiting to be found, and what opens the locked ones. The end-of-run card shows the road you took.

entries.title: The Endless Dungeon
entries.text: Endless is one dungeon now, made of regions: Greenshore Fields, Bandit Camp, Bandit Town, the Cyclops Arena and the Cultist Tower, plus the Dump once you beat the Garbage Man's third wave and the Slime Grotto once you reach wave 10 of the Slime King's pit. Each region ends in a chest, harder regions hold better chests (the Cultist Tower never pays less than a Masterwork Vault), and the hardest can pay an Arcane Vault or a Royal Chest. The deeper you go, the harder the regions get. The Garbage Man and the Slime King appear as gentler versions of themselves, and deep enemies hit less hard on a messy board. Co-op works too: regions either of you has opened can come up.

entries.title: Bosses make an entrance
entries.text: Every boss now arrives in style. The Bandit King spins down out of the sky and bounces onto his spot, the Slime King lands with a splat, the Cult Leader whirls out of a burst of dark magic, and the Garbage Man hops in with a bag balanced on his head. Shooty juggles his way on, until the last stone comes down on his head, and Punchy, Bernie and the Cyclops each have a move of their own. The fight starts exactly when it always did.

entries.title: Gel Packs
entries.text: A new block skin for anyone who maxes out a Slime King run, alone or with a friend: keep going until the game tells you the run has reached its limit. Pouches of coloured gel that squash flat when they land, bulge, and wobble back into place. Slam a piece down and the blocks underneath feel it too, and a line clear lands everything above it with a squish. Fights against him, and every fight, also run lighter: the health bars cost far less to draw while they move.

entries.title: Omens, and the Golden Slime King
entries.text: Now and then a Slime King walks in golden: beat him for three times his loot and up to 200 coins. And Endless and Dark have Omens. Open 30 chests in Endless or Dark to claim the Omen Seeker feat, then switch Omens on from the Endless and Dark cards. After every third chest an omen takes hold for a few kills: a boon like Wrath, Bounty or Gold Rush, a curse like Frenzy or Thick Hide, or a pact that makes the fight harder and pays far more. Every run with Omens on earns 20% more XP.

entries.title: The Slime King's new look
entries.text: The Slime King has a whole new body, crown and scowl, and his idol has a new look too: the Goop Idol is now the Ooze Idol, a hardened lump of his ooze, and the ring it makes is now the Oozing Ring. Anything you already own just changes its name. Royal Jelly now wears a little crown, and Thick Slime sits heavy and bubbling.

entries.title: A longer look round
entries.text: New adventurers who finish the tutorial can now ask to be shown more: every place to play, what each menu is for, and a line or two inside each screen that matters, from your gear to the Upgrade trees. Or say you'll figure it out, and go.

entries.title: Scrap in the Royal Vault
entries.text: The Slime King's Royal Vault can now hold 1 to 10 Scrap as well, now and then. And a vault with many rewards now lays its reels out in two columns, so every one of them and the Collect button stay on screen.

entries.title: Gear breaks in the Dark
entries.text: Dying to a monster in Dark Greenshore no longer takes everything you wear. Your gear breaks instead: it stays on you, drawn cracked and red, and gives a tenth of its stats until you mend it. Half the time the Dark also takes one piece, which may turn up in somebody's Dark chest. Build the new Repair Station beside your Smelter, then open a broken piece in your inventory and press Repair: a little of its main material and some Scrap make it whole. Its second and third levels mend tier-three and tier-four gear. Losing a fight to another player still costs what you wear.

entries.title: Friends
entries.text: A Friends button on the main menu. Add players by name, or from the people you shared a room, a party or a duel with this week. See who's online and what they're doing, then invite them straight into your private Farm room, co-op room or Arena fight: they get a card at the top of the screen and one click joins. You choose who can send you requests, whether you show as online, and whether you take invites at all, and a block always wins.

entries.title: Mastery feats
entries.text: Three new Feats with ten levels each, one for every fighting style. Deal damage with a sword, a bow or a staff to level its mastery, then claim each level on the Feats page for a stronger style bonus: combo clears for melee, triples and Quads for ranged, spins for magic, up to 12.5% more at level ten. The first level comes quickly; the last takes a very long time. You can also paste a room code into the code field now, and the Slime King's later walls no longer cover your board.

entries.title: Composts in versus
entries.text: Fertiliser and every compost now work in Farm Versus and Dark Farm. With some in your Boosts, each round you are dealt uses one and boosts what you gather that round, just like a Solo run. In Dark Farm the boost comes before the stake, so the winner takes a bigger haul.

entries.title: Check their gear
entries.text: Before a co-op run or an Arena duel, click any piece the other player is wearing to see its stats, what it sells for and its Forge roll. Enhanced gear shows its star beside its name. The Garbage Man's card now shows his Scrap price, lowered by Garbage Garrison. Transmuting into tier four now takes a Thick Slime instead of a Slime Gel, and Orichalcum Armor takes Duskhide instead of Rugged Hide.

entries.title: Six new Feats, and Arcane weeklies
entries.text: Six more Feats on the Upgrade menu, each a long road with a permanent reward at the end: double XP from the Farm, an extra Scrap from every tier-two or better piece you salvage, a free door into the Slime King's pit, merchants paying a quarter more, a second daily task swap, and five more Market listings. At level 50 the weekly task can pay the Arcane Vault, with asks to match. The Market now holds ten listings, fifteen with the Trading Post.

entries.title: The Collection Log
entries.text: A new book on the main menu, under Skins, lists everything every enemy can drop, boss by boss, with the odds for each. Every item stays a question mark until an enemy drops it for you, and a card pops up at the side of the screen the moment one does. Fill every page: each one turns green when it is complete, and the log counts your kills too.

entries.title: Deeper in the pit
entries.text: Royal Jelly keeps getting likelier the deeper you go, up to 40%. Every twentieth wave opens a Royal Vault with Thick Slime, Royal Jelly and refined materials, and the deeper the vault, the likelier its materials are tier four. Thick Slime also drops from wave ten on, and Super Compost now takes two Royal Jelly and a Thick Slime. The pit's card shows the best waves, solo and with a friend.

entries.title: A longer calm, and a price at the pit
entries.text: The calm between Slime Kings is now 15 seconds, so you have time to build back up before the next one. His pit now costs 100 Gold to enter, and with a friend you each pay your own.

entries.title: The Slime King
entries.text: A new dungeon with its own boss, alone or with a friend. He walls your board down to four columns until he falls, covers your tower in slime that soaks your clears, and wraps you up until you shake him off left and right. Every king you beat gives you a calm to build back up before the next one, stronger and faster. Dying in his pit loses nothing. He drops Slime Balls, Royal Jelly and the Goop Idol: cook Royal Slime Broth, mix Super Compost for the Farm, set the idol in a Ring of Goop, and stitch a Slime Bag that keeps three of your finds when a Dark run kills you.

entries.title: The Arcane Vault
entries.text: Beat the Garbage Man's tenth wave and you now open an Arcane Vault instead of a Masterwork Vault. It can hold Orichalcum Ingots, Darkwood Planks, Lotus Cloth and Duskhide, a new leather found nowhere else, which the lotus-lined archer's cap and tunic are now made from. From wave ten on, he can also drop raw Orichalcum Ore, Darkwood Logs and Lotus Leaves.

entries.title: Tier four gear
entries.text: Eleven new pieces to craft at level 50 from Orichalcum, Darkwood and Lotus: an Orichalcum Sword, Helmet, Armor and Buckler, a Darkwood Bow and Darkwood Staff, a Lotus Hat and Robe, a lotus-lined archer's cap and tunic, and the Lotus Tome, a spellbook for your off hand.

entries.title: Refine tier four
entries.text: Orichalcum Ore, Darkwood Logs and Lotus Leaves now refine into Orichalcum Ingots, Darkwood Planks and Lotus Cloth at level 50. The Master Refinery can also transmute tier-three materials into tier four, for Scrap. Four new Skills help you find more: Master Woodcutter, Master Miner and Master Farmer, and Veteran Gatherer, which grows with your level.

entries.title: Tier four on the Farm
entries.text: At level 50 you can build Mines, Trees and Plants to level 4. Each one grows a new, very rare material on the Farm: purple Orichalcum Ore, black Darkwood Logs and light purple Lotus Leaves. Start stockpiling them now. Refining, new skills and new gear made from them are coming.

entries.title: Freezes get reported
entries.text: If the game freezes or crashes, it now sends a report the next time you log in, so it can be fixed. The report says where you were and how the game was running. It never includes your password or email. You can turn it off in Settings, under Performance. In the desktop client, a frozen game also offers to reload instead of making you close it.

entries.title: Enhanced finds
entries.text: A Masterwork Vault can now hold a piece of starter gear that already carries a Forge roll. So can the Garbage Man's vault for beating his ten waves, and every wave you beat from wave ten on. It is grade I or II, and yours to reroll at the Forge.

entries.title: Enhanced gear is worth more
entries.text: An enhanced piece now salvages for more Scrap and sells to a shop for more Gold than a plain one: the higher its grade and the better its roll, the more. A top Bandit Blade sells for 165 Gold instead of 75. It is never more than the Scrap you put into rolling it.

entries.title: Forge rolls have grades
entries.text: Every Scrap Forge roll now lands on a grade, I to IV, and the piece shows it: Vampiric III, Keen IV. The star on the piece is its grade's colour, green, blue, purple or gold. Better gear rolls higher grades more often, and only gear from level 30 can reach IV. Pieces you already have moved up to the next grade, so none got worse.

entries.title: Twenty-seven new Forge rolls
entries.text: The Scrap Forge can now roll effects for every kind of gear: a weapon that staggers, an armour that hits back, a helmet that heals at Dark checkpoints, a ring that hits harder until you are touched, and many more. They work in duels at half strength.

entries.title: Forge rolls that pay
entries.text: Six new Scrap Forge rolls change what a run earns. Scholar adds experience. Gilded adds coins. Scavenger's finds Scrap on kills. Gambler's Charm can make a kill drop its loot twice, and Fortune does the same for champions. Blessed makes a chest's second reward likelier.

entries.title: New Forge rolls
entries.text: The Scrap Forge can now roll three more stat lines. Trained raises your weapon's own bonus from a helmet or necklace. Balanced adds Attack, Power and Armor at once. Reckless trades Armor for more Attack and Power. And an enhanced piece's star now shows its tier: green, blue, purple or gold.

entries.title: Composts
entries.text: Fertiliser now doubles every material a Solo Farm run gathers. Rich Compost doubles tier three, and a compost for each gathering skill makes a run mostly one material, doubled. Farm Fighter now adds 50% to every Farm material.

entries.title: Two new gathering skills
entries.text: Seasoned Gatherer raises your chance of tier-three materials on every line, and it keeps growing as you level. Signature Mastery makes a Finesse spin that strikes tier three give even more of it.

entries.title: Cheaper tier-three refining
entries.text: Ipe Planks, Adamantite Ingots and Nettle Fabric now take 25 raw materials instead of 50. Build the new Master Refinery to make them from 20, and to transmute tier-two materials into tier three for some Scrap.

entries.title: The Scrap Forge
entries.text: Build the Scrap Forge and spend Scrap to roll a modifier onto a piece of gear: more Attack, Power or Armor, or a chance to hit harder, heal, halve a hit, hurt what hits you, or heal on a kill. Enhanced gear gets a star and counts in duels too. Each roll on the same piece costs more, and the new roll replaces the old one.

entries.title: Ten challenge skins
entries.text: Ten new block skins you can't get by levelling: solid stacking cubes, glowing wireframes, candy, chrome, ice, a handheld green screen and more. Each one is earned by doing something hard, like ten Quads in one run, two Perfect Clears, or beating someone five levels above you in a duel. See what each one asks on the Skins screen.

entries.title: Treasure Seals, chest by chest
entries.text: A Treasure Seal now upgrades one chest instead of a whole run. Fill your seal slot and each of your next chests opens a tier better, one seal per chest, until the stack runs out. The chest tells you when it is sealed.

entries.title: Onslaught chests come sooner
entries.text: Once Endless turns into Onslaught, a reward chest now takes one boss fewer to reach: every second boss on your own or in Dark Greenshore, every third in co-op.

entries.title: Seals, bags and bandages
entries.text: Three new Boosts slots. Build the Sealwright to craft seals: a Warden's Seal insures your most valuable piece on the way into a Dark run or a risk duel, and a Treasure Seal makes every chest of a run one tier better. In the bag slot, a Rugged Satchel keeps the best thing you found when a Dark run kills you, and a Provisions Pouch packs one more food. And a Bandage Roll lets you stand your co-op partner up after their first fall with a single line, on full health.

entries.title: Slime Broth shields you
entries.text: Eat Slime Broth and the next attack against you is absorbed whole, a monster's or another player's. The Cookhouse's foods now heal a little less, every fish recipe needs Coal, and Minor Healing Potions cost more to brew and buy.

entries.title: The Cookhouse, the Smelter and the Trading Post
entries.text: Three new buildings for your base. The Cookhouse cooks Carrot Stew, Trout Pie and Slime Broth, foods that heal far more than a potion. The Smelter breaks spare gear down into Scrap. The Trading Post cuts the market's cut of your sales to 3% and lets you keep 30 listings up.

entries.title: Insure your gear
entries.text: Build the Warden's Vault and spend Scrap to insure one piece before a Dark run or a risk duel. Die or lose, and that piece stays with you.

entries.title: Boosts and Fertiliser
entries.text: Your equipment has a new Boosts tab, and nothing in it is lost when you die. Put Fertiliser there and every Solo Farm run gathers 15% more of everything.

entries.title: A welcome for new adventurers
entries.text: Every new account opens a Masterwork Vault, then a short tour starts you off on the Farm.

entries.title: Dark Greenshore checkpoints
entries.text: No more running out the back door. Every two rounds you reach a checkpoint: walk out with your haul, or press on and risk it all. And when more hunters are about, the next fight finds you when you least expect it.

entries.title: Sharper rotation
entries.text: The I piece now kicks off walls and turns 180 the way competitive stackers expect, and a piece on the ground can no longer be spun forever to stall.

entries.title: The Horned Staff
entries.text: Mages get a weapon to stand beside the Spiky Bow and the Kris: a staff crowned with the Cult Leader's horns.

entries.title: Boss weapons bite in PvP
entries.text: Land a Quad or a T-Spin with a Bandit Blade and the King's blade spin hits your rival's board. The Spiky Bow sends the Cult Leader's tentacle. And the Ring of Garbage now throws a slab of garbage you can see.

entries.title: Revive your co-op partner
entries.text: When your partner goes down, beat the challenge on your board to bring them back. New Mending skills heal them with S and Z spins.

entries.title: Your settings travel with you
entries.text: Log in anywhere and your handling, controls, font and skin come with you.

entries.title: Ring of Thorns
entries.text: Now hits a monster back for twice what it took, and the Garbage Man keeps your best wave.

entries.title: Jewellery
entries.text: Six idols, three amulets and three new rings.

entries.title: Feats
entries.text: Four permanent perks for the hardest deeds.

entries.title: The Ring of Garbage
entries.text: Clear big and the monster's next attack comes later.

entries.title: The Garbage Man
entries.text: A wave dungeon with its own boss.

entries.title: Co-op Endless
entries.text: Take on Endless with a friend.
